headline: Approved concept of signage at Kondelin Road entrance for Eastern Waste Services and DLM Properties
summary: The board approved, in concept, signage at the entrance to Kondelin Road requiring covered loads and no queuing, subject to final design approval. The meeting also covered Blackburn Industrial Park updates, Jodrey State Fish Pier capital needs, the I-4C2 project, and financial updates showing a balance of $514,000.00.
decisions: Approved, in concept, signage at the entrance of the industrial park subject to further Board review and final design approval by Eastern Waste Services.
Approved the concept of a sign at Kondelin Road stating all loads must be covered and no queuing is allowed, subject to final design and placement approval; roll call vote, all in favor.

plain_text:
1 
 
 
 
 
 
EDIC BOARD MEETING MINUTES 
Tuesday, August 11, 2026 at 4:30 pm. 
Harbor Master’s Conference Room 
19 Harbor Loop  
Gloucester, Ma 01930 
 
• Open Meeting Laws were read. Meeting began at 4:32 pm. 
• Roll call attendance was taken. In attendance: Chair Tom Balf, Treasurer Taylor Hedges, Rob Gordon, Patty 
Knaggs, and Jerrold Oppenheim. Absent: Gretel Seeley and Jonathan Katz. Also, in attendance were 
Attorney Adria Pratt, legal counsel to the EDIC Board and, Attorney Joel Favazza from Seaside Legal 
Solutions at 123 Main Street.  
• A motion was made to approve the June 9, 2026 meeting minutes. All were in favor  per roll call voice. 
• Attorney Favazza representing his clients Eastern Waste Services and DLM Properties explained to the 
EDIC Board that the City’s Board of Health required his client to request specific signage at the entrance to 
Kondelin Road, as a condition of their site assignment decision, that would indicate no uncovered loads 
and no queuing on Kondelin Road. Last August, Eastern Waste received a site assignment decision from 
the Board of Health allowing the Essex County Recycling Center and Hiltz Disposal Headquarters to 
upgrade the facility into a modern-day construction and demolition debris transfer station , if certain 
conditions were met, which included a myriad of conditions elating to traffic, pollution control, 
environmental controls, and noise. One of the long-standing conditions that is currently in place now for 
the existing facility is they do not allow uncovered loads.  
• Favazza shared with the Board a mock-up of a proposed sign to be placed at the entrance to Kondelin 
Road. The proposed signage is 24 inches by 18 inches. The Board agreed that the size, orientation, and the 
colors that are to be used should stand out to an incoming truck or trailer. Attorney Pratt added that she 
does not think that the current mockup is big enough to catch anyone’s attention. Attorney Favazza 
stated that they do not want to put something there that is massive and takes over the rest of the 
signage. He asked to hear the Board’s thoughts on sizing and placement.  The Board discussed sizing, 
placement, whether the sign should match the existing green signs or stand out with a different color, and 
whether other “safety or traffic policies” – relevant to all tenants – should be placed at the entrance. the 
Board voted to approve – in concept – signage at the entrance of the industrial park subject to further 
thinking of the Board regarding other relevant safety policies that they may wish to advertise and final 
Board approval of the design and placement by Eastern Waste Services.
2 
 
A motion was made to allow Eastern Waste Services to have some type of signage at the beginning of 
Kondelin Road that states all loads must be covered and no queuing is allowed. The EDIC Board voted to 
approve the concept of a sign subject to final approval of the design and placement.    
 
 Treasurer Hedges made the motion and a roll call vote was taken . All were in favor.  
 
• The meeting also covered updates on Blackburn Industrial Park expansion activities, plans for a tenant’s 
meeting on October 13th. The focus of the tenant’s meeting will be discussions regarding energy, updates 
from each company, job opportunities, and training. National Grid will also be invited to provide an 
update on power supply issues in the Park and in the greater Cape Ann area.   
• CATA has signaled its interest in accessing the current emergency road at the end of Pond Road to gain 
direct access to Blackburn Industrial Park. Use of this entrance could significantly reduce  the commute 
between Pond Road and Blackburn Industrial Park. Chair Balf added that this could also be discussed at 
the tenant meeting.  
• Jodrey State Fish Pier. Chair Balf spoke to the Board about a positive meeting with Mass Development 
regarding the State Pier. MassDevelopment shared with us their updated Capital Needs Assessment.  The 
priority needs at the Jodrey State Fish Pier include a freezer unit/Condenser in Building #1 and new roof 
for Building #3. Identified costs for the fish pier are projected to 2070 which are estimated at $25 million 
dollars, 75% of which are wharves and piers and other maritime infrastructure needs. It was a very 
productive meeting. The EDIC and Mass Development agreed to meet quarterly.  City representatives, the 
EDIC, and Mass Development plan on meeting next month in September to discuss the City’s Municipal 
Harbor Plan. Mass Development would like to get a better understanding of the Municipal Harbor Plan  so 
they have a better context for what Gloucester would like to see its harbor look like in the years moving 
forward and identify where there are economic development opportunities.  It was also agreed that an 
all-tenants meeting will be planned for later this year or early 2027.  After recent meetings with the 
Secretary and Undersecretary of Economic Development, there appears to be an opportunity for 
state/City collaboration, planning, and investment. 
• Balf briefly updated the Board on the I-4C2 project and its potential contract extension. The goal is to 
finalize a document requesting interest in the development of the property from developers, maritime 
operators, and other water-dependent users and administer that process. 
• The Workforce Training Sub-committee will provide an update to the Board at the September meeting.  
• Financial update: Treasurer Hedges confirmed that all of the landscaping payments have been made 
except one that is still outstanding. Treasurer Hedges will follow up with that company. The EDIC is 
currently has a balance of $514,000.00.  
• Next meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 8th, 2026.  
• A motion was made to adjourn. All were in favor. 
• The meeting concluded at 5:19 pm.
